s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement following vaccination
salient_findings: Fever and erythema on trunk and extremities after vaccination
Elevated inflammatory markers and abnormal laboratory tests
Imaging findings of hepatosplenomegaly, coronary artery occlusion, and vascular lesions
key_facts: 22-year-old Japanese man with no medical history or family history
Developed fever and erythema 3 days after receiving first dose of Moderna vaccine
Developed fever on the 12th day after second vaccination
Initial symptoms gradually worsened leading to hospitalization on the 24th day after second vaccination
Imaging findings of hepatosplenomegaly and coronary artery occlusion
SARS-CoV-2 PCR test results were repeatedly negative

differentials: Tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome (TRAPS)
per_call: Tumor necrosis factor receptor-associated periodic syndrome (TRAPS)

shortlist.label: Kawasaki disease
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement following vaccination, with fever, erythema, and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C)
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to Kawasaki disease, with systemic inflammation and multi-organ involvement following vaccination

shortlist.label: Vaccine-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (VITT)
shortlist.why_kept: Thrombocytopenia and thrombosis observed in the patient, which could be related to the vaccination

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum ferritin and triglycerides, and hemophagocytosis observed in the bone marrow, which are characteristic of HLH

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Involvement of large arteries, including the coronary arteries, and elevated inflammatory markers, which are consistent with Takayasu arteritis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, erythema, and elevated inflammatory markers, along with the temporal relationship to the Moderna vaccine, are consistent with MIS-C. The patient's age and lack of medical history also support this diagnosis, as MIS-C has been reported in young adults with no prior medical conditions.

rejected.label: Kawasaki disease
rejected.why: While Kawasaki disease shares some similarities with MIS-C, the patient's age and the presence of coronary artery occlusion and thrombocytopenia on readmission are more consistent with MIS-C.

rejected.label: Vaccine-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (VITT)
rejected.why: VITT typically presents with thrombocytopenia and thrombosis, but the patient's initial platelet count was normal, and the thrombocytopenia on readmission may be a consequence of the underlying inflammatory process.

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)
rejected.why: HLH is a rare condition characterized by hemophagocytosis, which was not reported in the patient's laboratory results or imaging studies.

rejected.label: Takayasu arteritis
rejected.why: Takayasu arteritis is a large vessel vasculitis that typically presents with symptoms of vascular insufficiency, which were not reported in the patient's case.

gold: Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome after SARS-CoV-2 vaccination (MIS-V) with myocardial infarction
